evidence_status: Public research through 2026-09-12. Future actions and outcomes are a model simulation. No actual pilot store or customer records are supplied.
measurement_rule: Null means unmeasured. Keep real measurement fields null and complete observed sample counts at zero without sourced operating records. Put hypothetical estimates in separately named simulated_* fields with assumptions, never in observed fields. Maintain a concise public_strategy_history of observable implemented actions and consequences so later players can adapt. Do not publish private budgets, dossiers or unseen internal intentions. Advance calendar_period to the end of the current month.
public_market_context: Starbucks is investing in coffeehouse service, staffing and Smart Queue while US transactions are growing. Dutch Bros offers drive-through beverages and Order Ahead at participating shops. Dunkin offers coffee-and-food value and mobile ordering through a franchise network. Some morning purchases can shift to home preparation or disappear. Local overlaps and customer segments in this exercise are assumptions.
public_strategy_history: January 2027: Starbucks launches peak-hour mobile pickup slot limits and reserves 20% of capacity for in-café orders in 50 pilot cafés. Instrumentation begins for pilot and comparison cafés.

January 2027: Dunkin launches a $6 breakfast Meal Deal bundle in 15 consenting franchise stores near pilot cafés, with app promotion and local marketing. Store-level stop rules and monitoring are in place.
January 2027: Dutch Bros launches a geo-fenced digital campaign promoting Order Ahead and a $1 credit for first-time users in 12 shops, with peak-hour staffing adjustments and messaging.

January 2027: Morning customer segments respond: commuters abandon delayed Starbucks mobile orders, habitual app users tolerate limited delays but may switch after repeated issues, and café visitors continue in-person orders expecting improved experience.
